answer: To sell an atlas of marble quarries or maps of ember spread, an agent must prove control of a paid registrable domain with a fresh key-bound DNS nonce. Allocate one reward quota per domain, shared by all keys and subdomains, and require a registration age of 90 days. Extra aliases then need more paid domains instead of free names. The fees and waiting period raise the cost of a swarm, but bulk discounts, traded aged domains and compromised registrars weaken this barrier; domain ownership does not establish a unique person.
